SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - MAY 15, 2023 - 07:00 P.M.
SIERRA ROOM - CERRITOS CENTER FOR THE PERFORMING ARTS
18000 PARK PLAZA DRIVE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Sierra Room.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD MONDAY, MAY
15, 2023, 7:00 P.M., IN THE SIERRA ROOM AT CERRITOS CENTER FOR THE PERFORMING
ARTS, 18000 PARK PLAZA DRIVE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Pro Tem Solanki.

3.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Chuong Vo
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Bruce W. Barrows

4.  New Business

4A.  Review and consideration of the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Preliminary Combined Financial
  Program for the City of Cerritos and the Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment
  Agency (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  City Attorney Bill Ihrke provided information related to potential conflicts of interest
  related to Councilmember Johnson’s participation in budget discussions concerning the
  City’s agreement for law enforcement services with Councilmember Johnson’s employer,
  the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department.

  A staff report was given by Peter Kemp, Budget Manager. A PowerPoint presentation was
  displayed.

  CONSENSUS (Johnson): Directed the City Manager to: 1. Take action to ensure the
  Cerritos Regional Chamber of Commerce (Chamber) is in compliance with the City’s
  reporting policies and requirements for the City community support program; and 2.
  Request the Chamber provide detail as to how the FY 2022-23 amount ($40K) was utilized
  and justification for the additional amount ($22K) requested for FY 2023-24 (total request
  was $62K).

  Prior to the commencement of discussion of various law enforcement related budget items,
  Councilmember Johnson recused herself from participation. She left her seat at the dais
  and exited the Council Chamber. Upon conclusion of discussion of the aforementioned
  items, Councilmember Johnson entered the Council Chamber and resumed her seat at the
  dais for the remainder of the meeting.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to provide a report to the City Council on
  the feasibility of implementing use of driving golf carts and an online reservation system at
  the Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine Golf Course, if possible by the June 12 budget study session or
  at the earliest possible date thereafter, and once reviewed by the City Council, the matter
  may be referred to the Parks and Recreation Commission for further evaluation.

4.  New Business (continued)

4A.  (continued)

  CONSENSUS (Johnson): Directed the City Manager to provide a report to the City Council
  on the feasibility of hiring a specialized consultant to examine current CCPA marketing and
  advertising practices and provide recommendations on updated best practices and
  strategies.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to conduct a Family Arts Festival/CCPA 30th
  anniversary celebration event on September 24, 2023, in the proposed amount of
  approximately $50,000, at no final net budgetary cost to the City, as financially supported
  through external sponsorships, grants, and fundraising.

  The previous Consensus item was replaced by the following Consensus item:

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to conduct a Family Arts
  Festival/CCPA 30th anniversary celebration event on September 24, 2023, in the proposed
  amount of approximately $50,000, to be funded through the CCPA Endowment fund
  (Endowment), and replenish the Endowment through any external sponsorships, grants,
  and fundraising received.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written Correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record. Full-text copies of submitted written
  correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer.)

  Helen Evans submitted comments in opposition to making Cerritos a “Smart City.”

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period closed.

  There was no further action taken on this item.

5.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 9:57 p.m.
